ARTIST.expert-ux:
Creativity and precision define my work — I am a pixel-perfect UX/UI designer with a passion for crafting immersive digital experiences. Inspired by the surreal universe of Magritte, I bring a unique artistic touch to my designs, blending 2D and 3D visuals with a deep focus on user experience.

My key skills and expertise:
ARTIST.skill-1: UX/UI Design: Focus on user-centered, interactive, and aesthetic interfaces.
ARTIST.skill-2: Interactive Prototyping with Figma, Adobe XD, Zeplin, and Illustrator for engaging and dynamic mockups.
ARTIST.skill-3: 2D & 3D Design: Logo creation, 3D modeling, and immersive visual experiences with 3ds Max.
ARTIST.skill-4: Front-End Development: Expertise in Angular, React.js, Vue.js, TypeScript, SCSS, SASS.
ARTIST.skill-5: Responsive & Animated UI: Ensuring smooth interactions and seamless performance across devices.
ARTIST.expert-last:
I hold a Master’s degree in Computer Science from the University of Namur (graduated with distinction), combining technical expertise with a deep understanding of design.

One of my most exciting projects was developing a chatbot for an escape game as part of my Master’s thesis—demonstrating my ability to merge design and technology to create engaging digital experiences.
ARTIST.music:
Music is my passion, and I've been playing piano since I was 10. As a singer, I’m lucky to be coached by Aurore Sorce, a talented artist who excelled at the conservatory and closely guides me on my vocal journey.

I love performing covers of artists like Lana Del Rey, Lady Gaga, and Céline Dion, bringing emotion and creativity to every note.

You can find some of my covers on Instagram and YouTube. Check the link in the footer!
ARTIST.aboutme: Curious about who I am? Explore my journey, the languages I speak, and my passion for music through piano and singing. Dive deeper into what drives me and how it influences both my work and creativity.

ARTIST.resume-animal: Animal welfare is close to my heart. Sterilization and responsible adoption help reduce suffering and protect abandoned animals.
ARTIST.animal-1:
Animal welfare is a cause close to my heart. ❤️

Every day, associations and volunteers work tirelessly to improve the lives of abandoned animals. Their dedication is admirable, yet too many cats and dogs are still left to fend for themselves without a sustainable solution.
ARTIST.animal-2: One of the key solutions to this issue is sterilization. The overpopulation of stray cats is difficult to manage, leading to unnecessary suffering. Sterilization is a simple but crucial step in preventing this problem and improving animal welfare.
ARTIST.animal-3: We should also consider the condition of horses used for tourist rides. Instead of exploiting these animals for entertainment, motorized alternatives exist that can prevent their physical suffering.
ARTIST.animal-4: Animals are not just companions; they feel fear, pain, and deserve our respect. Everyone can play a role in their well-being by adopting more responsible behaviors.
ARTIST.animal-5:
I have personally adopted two cats, Batman and Lisa, who bring so much joy to my life.
On this topic, I highly recommend the film Flow, a silent yet deeply moving piece that beautifully portrays the sensitivity of animals. The black cat in the movie reminds me so much of my Batman, a loyal and charismatic companion!
ARTIST.animal-6: To learn more about feline overpopulation and GAIA’s campaign, you can visit this link: GAIA Campaign
ARTIST.resume-human: A small act of kindness can make a big difference. Helping others and protecting our planet starts with simple, everyday actions.
ARTIST.human-1:
A simple smile costs nothing and can brighten someone's day. 😊

In a world where many struggle with poverty and injustice, every action counts.
It is essential to think of others and take action, even in small ways, to create a more compassionate future.
ARTIST.human-2:
Thousands of organizations work every day to improve the lives of those in need.
Even a small donation can make a real difference. Here are some organizations striving for a better world:
  • UNICEF - Supporting children and their rights.
  • SOS Children's Villages - Protecting and educating vulnerable children.
  • Red Cross - Emergency relief and humanitarian aid.
ARTIST.human-3:
Our planet also needs us. 🌍 Small, simple actions can have a big impact:
  • Throwing waste in the bin instead of littering.
  • Turning off the water while soaping up in the shower to avoid waste.
  • Reducing food waste by adjusting portion sizes.
ARTIST.human-4:
Helping others and protecting the environment isn’t difficult. Let’s work together to be kinder and more responsible.

❤️ Thank you for these small actions that, combined, can change the world.
ARTIST.resume-contact: Feel free to reach out for collaborations or questions. Let’s create something amazing together!

UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.intro: UX analysis of the interactive game Ganesha Sudoku, from initial concept to visual design and overall experience improvements.
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.tech.title: Context & Motivation
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.tech.desc: After testing various Sudoku games on smartphones and observing what worked (or didn’t) in terms of usability, I took on a personal challenge to create my own version, exploring both visual and interaction aspects.
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.structure.title: Functional Prototype
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.structure.desc:
Before focusing on aesthetics, my priority was to make the game fully functional :

  • Grid generation
  • Player input validation
  • Rule compliance checking

This approach ensured a solid foundation before the visual layer was added.
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.generation.title: Grid Generation Logic
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.generation.desc:
To ensure that all grids were always valid and solvable, I used an algorithmic approach known as backtracking. This method :

  • Builds the grid step by step
  • Tests each number placement
  • Backtracks whenever a constraint isn’t met

This process is like navigating a maze: moving forward when possible and stepping back when blocked, ensuring a conflict‑free solution.
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.uiux.title: UX/UI Approach
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.uiux.desc:
Once the core logic was established, I designed the mocks in Figma, using a modern and intuitive aesthetic. Visual influences borrowed from Squid Game were adapted for a bold yet clear presentation.

Key focus areas included :

  • Cell readability
  • Visual hierarchy
  • Interactive feedback for player actions
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.methods.title: Interaction Enhancements
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.methods.desc:
From early tests I added features to enhance the experience :

  • A remaining numbers counter
  • Time tracking for immersion
  • A rules section for guidance

These additions improve clarity and increase player engagement.
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.deployment.title: Responsive & Mobile‑First
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.deployment.desc: The interface was designed with a mobile‑first mindset to ensure a smooth experience on phones, then adapted for desktop while maintaining simple and intuitive navigation.
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.responsive.title: User Testing & Iterations
UX_CASE_GANESHA_SUDOKU.responsive.desc:
Friends tested the game on various devices. Their feedback helped :

  • Fix bugs
  • Adjust visual elements
  • Improve clarity of interactions

These iterations delivered a more seamless, friction‑free experience.

UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.intro: UX analysis of the interactive game Battleship, from initial inspiration to visual and functional design, focusing on an immersive maritime identity and experience.
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.tech.title: Context & Inspirations
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.tech.desc: Before designing the interface, I reviewed multiple smartphone versions of Battleship to understand how players interact with grids and perceive action. The visual theme draws from the ocean and submarines, including a zoom/blur effect around the periscope to reinforce immersion.
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.structure.title: Ship Placement & Interaction
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.structure.desc:
The experience begins with ship placement. To prevent errors, the interface guides the user with clear rules :

  • Ships cannot extend beyond grid borders
  • They must not overlap
  • Visual indicators validate placements

This UX step ensures intuitive and frustration‑free interaction.
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.generation.title: AI Grid Generation
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.generation.desc:
Unlike Sudoku, the computer grid in this game doesn’t use backtracking. The AI places ships by checking adjacent cells in four directions (North, South, East, West) to simulate more human‑like and intelligent logic while respecting game constraints.

This ensures coherent placement without overlaps or off‑grid positions and keeps each game unique.
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.uiux.title: UI Approach
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.uiux.desc:
To strengthen the maritime atmosphere, I incorporated visuals inspired by submarine themes :

  • A deep blue and turquoise color palette
  • Blur effects around the periscope to evoke focus and exploration
  • Smooth transitions and visual feedback throughout play

This helps players feel the environment while keeping the interface clear and readable.
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.methods.title: Feedback & UX Iterations
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.methods.desc:
During early tests I observed player reactions to placements and visual feedback. Insights led to improvements in animations, indication colors (valid vs invalid), and the introduction of smoother micro‑interactions.

These iterations improved engagement and reduced placement errors.
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.deployment.title: Responsive & Cross‑Platform
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.deployment.desc: The interface was designed to be fully responsive, delivering a smooth experience on both mobile and desktop without loss of readability or interactive feedback.
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.testing.title: User Testing & Refinements
UX_CASE_GANESHA_BATTLEFIELD.testing.desc:
Friend testers and several participants tried the game on multiple devices. Their feedback helped :

  • Improve the ship placement logic
  • Adjust interactive areas
  • Clarify transitions between game states

These insights were invaluable in improving clarity and overall ergonomics.
